subject: API protection vendor shortlist and savings playbook
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: API protection vendor shortlist and savings playbook

Team —

We’re 90 days out from the current CDN/WAF commitments rolling into the next fiscal quarter. I want a concise vendor shortlist + a one-page savings playbook we can take to GTM and finance. Goal: identify 2 mandatory requirements (regional POP coverage and managed rules SLA), 3 buying levers (commit, term, feature bundling), and a conservative run-rate savings estimate vs current spend.

Please kick this off:
- Marissa: lead vendor shortlist + RFX template and run a first-pass feature comparison.
- Marcus: pull the last 12 months of token/edge usage and produce a quick $/month baseline; add any preliminary vendor discounts you’ve heard.
- Laura: highlight contracting knobs we should keep (indemnity, data residency, incident MTTR SLA).

Attachments: edge_contracts_summary.xlsx, current_usage_report.pdf (baseline data).

Deliverable: one-page playbook + shortlist by EOD Monday (we’ll use it to invite vendors to an RFP/technical bake-off). I’ll schedule a 30m sync once we have the draft.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API protection vendor shortlist and savings playbook

Thanks — on it. Quick notes from an initial pass:

- Candidate shortlist (first cut): Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai, and a smaller specialist (SignalEdge) for managed WAF only. I prioritized global POPs, serverless integration, and dev-friendly routing.
- Must-have checklist idea: regional POPs (NA/EU/APAC), per-route rate limiting, managed rules updates, SOC2 + penetration test cadence, ability to host custom Lua/WASM rules.
- Preference: prioritize vendors that offer both CDN + WAF as a single package (simpler ops).

I attached an RFX template (rfx_template.docx) that we can reuse. Marcus — can you drop the usage slices you’ll use (p95 vs avg, origin egress)? Need those to model commit tiers. Laura — any immediate legal red flags on the shortlist?

I’ll assemble a side-by-side feature matrix and a one-page playbook draft by Monday morning.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Edge
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API protection vendor shortlist and savings playbook

Attached is a vendor_quote_matrix.csv with my first-pass numbers based on our trailing 12mo usage (see current_usage_report.pdf):

Summary (high level):
- Cloudflare: sticker is similar to today; they offered an early-commit discount ~15–20% if we take a 12–24 month reserved plan plus bundled WAF managed rules. Good POP coverage for EU/APAC.
- Fastly: has flexible reserved capacity (commit + burst); initial pricing for our profile shows potential savings of ~10–18% if we normalize cache-hit improvements and offload. Fastly asked about our average concurrent connections; I fed p95 numbers.
- Akamai: premium pricing but includes enterprise support + advanced bot management; potential savings require a longer term or volume-based negotiation.
- SignalEdge (specialist): much lower sticker for managed WAF but no global CDN — would be an overlay procurement.

Assumptions are in the sheet. Key risk: our spike patterns (growth days) are responsible for ~35% of cost; committing to a low tier could blow up during launches. We should model a hybrid (primary CDN with a WAF overlay) and a full consolidation scenario.

Attachments: vendor_quote_matrix.csv

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API protection vendor shortlist and savings playbook

Thanks for the drafts — a few contracting items to call out before we engage vendors externally:

1) Evidence & compliance: Request SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary up front. If data residency is required for any product flow (EU regulated accounts), flag that early.
2) SLAs and credits: define MTTR and a tokenized latency SLA for critical routes. Avoid open-ended indemnities around customer data unless we get reciprocal limits.
3) Term & termination: prefer a 12–24 month term with a 30–60 day operational exit clause tied to cache retention and KV cache migration support.
4) Security review timeline: security will need 10 business days to evaluate vendor artifact package; procurement needs 5 business days to review contract redlines.

Procurement process: we’ll open a purchase request with the vendors we invite. I created a procurement intake ticket and added the Drive RFP folder to it. DocuSign template for a preliminary NDA + short-form SOW is at the DocuSign link in thread metadata.

If we want external vendor demos prior to issuing the RFP, I recommend limiting to 30 minutes and only invite two vendors per slot.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal & Procurement
Redwood Inference

Team + vendor partners —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. We’ll do the following next:

1) Internal: Marissa — finalize the one-page playbook and the feature matrix by EOD Friday. Marcus — finalize the cost model and produce a commit vs on-demand sensitivity table. Laura — queue the security artifact request template and procurement ticket.

2) Vendors: we’re scheduling a two-week RFP window. I’m inviting Cloudflare, Fastly, and Akamai to bid; we’ll keep SignalEdge as a possible managed-WAF overlay if bids are competitive. Expect an RFP doc (Drive link) by Monday and a vendor Q&A slot next Thursday (30m).

3) Decision criteria (tentative): 40% cost (TCO over 12 mo), 30% operational fit (dev ergonomics + rules management), 20% reliability/SLA, 10% security/compliance posture.

Attachments: RFP Drive link (see metadata). Please add any further constraints in the Drive doc. I’ll set the RFP invite calendar after Marissa publishes the playbook.

Thanks — will loop back with calendar invites shortly.

Vivek
VP, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference
